---
title: "A factor keeps its levels after filtering"
ref: FCT-03
categories: [Factors]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'nlevels(factor(c("a", "b"))[1])'
reponse: '2'
attendu: "`1`, only the value a is left"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
f <- factor(c("a", "b"))[1]
f
levels(f)
table(f)
```
:::

## Why

Extracting part of a factor leaves its table of levels untouched. Level `b` no longer has any value, but it is still declared.

It then shows up wherever levels matter: a cell at 0 in `table()`, an empty bar in a plot, a category with no observation in a model, or an empty group in `split()`.

## The remedy

Drop unused levels with `droplevels()` after filtering.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
f <- droplevels(f)
levels(f)
table(f)
```
:::
